I mostly use my bottles in the house, so I’m not really worried about damaging them. The boot is just shy of two inches tall, so I can’t imagine it would protect from damage on the upper body of a flask.

None of my bottles are from a name brand, just random ones I’ve acquired. The boot is a little loose on slim body bottles, but it fits. On bottles where the boot fits tightly, I just rolled the sides down to peel it off when I was done.

The bottom of the silicone feels reinforced and a little thicker than the sides.

The rainbow print is not aligned perfectly on the seam, which bugs me. The color stripes are not perfectly horizontal either, they are a little wavy in some spots. I also have a small black spot in the print on mine, and the red stripe looks like it might peel after extended use.

The boot has a faint plastic scent that did not fade after washing.

text_fidelity_a:
Chase 8 Bike Hydration Vest - Integrated Tool Organization - 70 oz I traded out a perfectly good riding hydration pack made by another company to go with Camelbak, which is a company I very much like. I have a different pack ready to go for each of my major outdoor hobbies. This one for biking, of course.

One negative is that the other brand actually had an easier to fill, empty, and dry hydration pack. For some reason, Camelbak keeps changing theirs, and not always for the better: this one no longer has the little plastic pieces that flip out from around the circular fill area which - on my other recent models - helped the reservoir to drain and dry out easier. Since this does not have that feature, it stays flat, making it harder to dry, and it still has the rib inside the pack which keeps you from reaching in all the way to dry it out with a towel. All that said, the other-branded pack had a bit of a goofy tube that could kink and never quite looked or felt right.

But...another negative for the Camelbak - the reservoir from the other branded-pack came with a mouthpiece cover, whereas I have to buy yet another for use with this Camelbak. That should just come with because ...well, I've just been in too many disgusting places to not want to ensure my mouthpiece is covered. Even though the mouthpiece has changed, it does seem that the same covers will fit.

Weight and comfort are about perfect on this thing. And it holds what I need it to. Here is how I ride: In the front mini-compartment with the odd closure, I keep the stuff that's sort of permanent and hopefully I won't need often - my bike multi-tool, some small stuff to fix tires, and a spare tire. Also some sealing bags to put my phone and wallet in should it rain.

The main compartment I keep my tire pump, as my last pack had a spot for it and I like that better than having more crap on my actual bike. Also biking gloves. The other day, I comfortably had my sunglasses case and coffee mug in there as well.

I had the 2l reservoir almost full with all this. It was full, but totally fine. I also used the "stretch pocket" for my very compact wind-breaker once it was all wet and dirty, but I was too hot to wear it.

In the front zip pocket, I kept my keys and phone. Great place for them, since I compulsively check for them and this also allows for access to your phone if you need to take a pic or something. I would have liked a specific latch or zip pocket for keys...it does have net pocket for that that seems appropriate, but a zipper would be better. I don't want to worry there is any possibility such a thing could slip out.

I also keep my biking GPS in the other mesh pocket when it's not on my bike.

Once you get the straps just how you need them (and note that you may have to adjust them if you add or subtract a lot of gear), this pack manages to feel so streamlined that it is almost a part of you. It's up high on your back and tight against you all around. No air channels in the back except for some minor mesh, so it stays light and streamlined. 2 front straps built in keep a nice grip without a lot of extra straps getting in the way.

Although it says unisex, I'm not sure this is great for women. I know a lot of women's Camelbaks have straps built a certain way to avoid breasts, but these are all over my chest, so I'm not sure it would be comfortable for a woman (but I really wouldn't know).

Also, I'm not sure if huge dudes could wear this comfortably. I am ~73.5", 185 lbs., and I have my chest straps about as loose as they can be made, although I have a bit of room left on the back straps. It's hard for me to tell how far that will go in the chest area.

The zippers and seams are well hidden making this great for people who want a sleek and simple design, while still being of obvious quality.

It also seems to be water resistant, as none of my stuff got wet the other day in a brief but heavy rain.

The only thing that had bothered me while riding was the tube was noticeable behind my head. But now I just realized the tube can go in either side, so that point becomes moot!

Overall, an excellent pack. Perfect for my half-day biking needs.
text_fidelity_b: Chase 8 Bike Hydration Vest - Integrated Tool Organization - 70 oz

Kijaro Dual Lock Folding Chair I'm very pleased with this folding chair. It's far more comfortable than I thought it would be. The mesh and fabric are suspended from the frame, so you never get the hard poke of a metal bar when you're sitting. My back is pretty sensitive to poor seating situations, but I can sit in this for quite some time without any discomfort.

Lots of nicely thought out design features, such as cup holders in each arm, wide fabric on the arms for comfort no matter how you position your arms, and a very easy-to-use folding feature.

The fabric is tough. It's not indestructible, but I expect to be able to get years of use out of it without having to baby it. The frame is also sturdy - no wiggles or wobbles when it fully unfolded. Granted, this type of construction makes the chair heavier than than other folding chairs, but I'm more than happy to deal with a little extra weight in exchange for comfort and solid construction.

My only quibble is that the seat is very wide - about 22 inches at the back and 24 inches at the widest part at the front. A narrower sear width would be nice, and would also allow the chair to take up less room when it's in use. But, better to have it too wide than not wide enough.

Great choice if you're looking for a comfortable folding chair.

text_fidelity_a:
Kryptonite Keeper 785 Integrated Bicycle Lock Chain Bike Lock, 33.5-Inch, Red Bicycle locks come in lots of different strength/security levels. This is not a great lock. If you look at Kryptonite's web site, this is their cheapest and lightest weight chain lock. They give it a 5 out 10 rating. The Kryptonite Evolution chain lock gets an 8/10 rating and the Kryptonite New York chain gets a 10/10 rating. Those are both heavier and more expensive locks.

This Keeper lock is probably OK for lower risk situations, like daytime use at school or for short trips to the supermarket or a restaurant. It's also OK in rurals areas etc where there aren't a lot of bike thieves. This lock is much better than a cable lock (which mostly can be cut with small wire cutters), but a thief can probably still cut this with a heavy duty bolt cutter.

In the big city, this lock is far from sufficient as your only lock. Get a heavy duty lock as your primary lock (for your frame and rear wheel) and maybe use this as a secondary lock (for your front wheel).
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite Keeper 785 Integrated Bicycle Lock Chain Bike Lock, 33.5-Inch, Red

ONWEGO Camping Pillow/Inflatable Air Pillow- 20in x 12in, 10.5oz, Self Inflating, Compressible- Best for Outdoor Trips, Backpacking, Hiking, Beach, Travel, Motorcycle, Car Wow - this travel pillow is actually very comfortable and practical! We love to go camping and this pillow is perfect because it doesn't take up much space at all and it's very easy to use (and feels marvelous). Seriously, I tried bringing along regular pillows but they're too bulky and get dirty, and other inflatable pillows I've tried were usually too hard, too slippery, and just not comfortable enough for me to sleep on.

This self-inflating pillow reminds me of a sleep number bed because you can inflate it all the way then blow into it to make it a bit more firm or open the value and push air out until it feels just right. This is the first time I've been able to customize a pillow to suit my comfort level and I love it! The pillow has a soft feeling front side that feels cooling and comfortable enough, but I'd probably use a pillowcase just because I'm more accustomed to sleeping on one. The back side of the pillow has a textured material that helps hold it in place while I sleep so it doesn't slide out from under me.

It comes all rolled up and bound by a wide elastic band in a nylon storage case and measures 5.5in x 6in (when rolled up) and weighs just 10.5oz, so it's small and light enough to pack in your camping gear or in a carry on bag for use while flying. Removed from the bag and unrolled it looks like a dehydrated flattened rectangle, but if you push down on it you can feel a memory foam layer throughout the pillow's center, and I didn't detect any odor at all from it.

Once you open the valve on the end air begins to flow into it and it begins to self-inflate and expand. The manufacturer recommends that you let it sit inflated for 12-24 hours, allowing the foam core to expand fully. Once the foam has regained it's shape, your pillow will self-inflate to a comfortable firmness. It can inflate to a maximum size of 20in x 12in, and you can control how firm you want it to be by blowing gently into the pillows air valve to increase loft and firmness or opening the value and pushing air out of the pillow until it's as soft as you like. I LOVE being able to customize my pillow to find just the right loft and firmness level!

The pillow's top feels soft and smooth, and it's made of some outdoor-grade moisture resistant materials, so it should last a long time as well. It has an indentation in the center for your head which feels wonderful. To maintain it just wipe it off with soap and water. I was very pleased by the ease of deflating this travel pillow too. Just open the valve and begin to roll the pillow up to push the air back out. Once you've finished rolling it up, just fold the two long sizes together, keep squeezing the residual air out as you roll it that way, then place the elastic band back around it and slip it back into its storage bag. YES it actually is easy to roll up tight enough to fit back into its carry bag!

This pillow would be great to take along anywhere you want to have a comfortable pillow, like on a cruise, an airline flight, or anywhere you can fit the storage bag without losing too much packing space. I'm going to enjoy using it for family camping trips and as an occasional extra pillow when the girls have sleepovers and we need one for one of the kids. The only change I wish the manufacturer would make would be to attach the elastic band to the pillow somehow so it couldn't get misplaced. Otherwise, this travel pillow is perfect!

What you can't tell from the pictures is that because of the thicker nylon and the fact that there are two chairs, this is a fairly heavy product. text_fidelity_a:
MIAODAM Exercise Wheel and Resistance Band Ordered these for my son who’s struggled through quarantine to get an appropriate work out.. I know, I know- we’re all singing the same sad quarantine song (some in better tune than others-ha-ah!) This was an all inclusive workout set sold at a decent price point and although we had high hopes it would be as great as our gym membership.. (yeah, right!! We all need realistic expectations ..) this had its perks and drawback- ultimately, I would have liked to rate it 3.5 star. I would suggest this is set mean for beginners/novice level exercise enthusiast.. and could meet those needs fairly well. (Used 2-3x week and for 15-30min. at a time..) However, this might fall short for those expecting a little more from their equipment..

If purchasing keep in mind:

-The grip handles are smaller than some adult male hands..(at least in our house!) Obviously, this could prove problematic if.. ones grip is compromised right from the start. However, an adult females hand seems to fit the grip without issue.

-As with any elastic band the stretch is tighter when you begin. This set offers varied resistance (clearly marked by color) after x30 day use.. Lower resistance bands are showing more signs of “slack.” (Nothing has snapped on us! But, the lesser band is much easier to pull.. and I would beg to differ it’s because we’re getting so much stronger!!) Higher levels still have plenty of resistance but, we haven’t used nearly as much so, they stretch out - just something to keep in mind.

-Protect door jam with extra padding!! As these are braced against “wood” with a soft rounded ball, we have found- not all door jams are created equal (i’m pretty sure our door jams are made of wood composite?!!) So, be careful and add a small cut out of foam, washcloth or dish towel.. Anything you can easily rig to buffer The wall and protect it- bc, we noticed small indents being left on the door jam itself- not what we wanted and overtime without protection… It’ll only get worse!

-Appreciate the bag this came with to store all the items in along with the extra straps/gadgets. This does have instructions- however, they’re a bit tricky to read- just know you can Google a “how to video“ and obtain the info. easily enough . Would have loved to see this set contain added buffer pad for walls.. even a few photos with instructions- possibly something included in the future? I’d also appreciate including a magic eraser for the walls! The black rubber can leave small markings… Yes! These easily come off with wall eraser- Hence, the perk of including one in the bag!

Overall, this is not a bad set up. It can give a person- a good resistance workout.. It just has a few idiosyncrasies to work around.. I suggest knowing your audience and their physical size and ability… If, you do prior to any ordering- and are sure to protect the physical structure of the door when setting up- then, one should get what you need from this workout set.

I hope this info helps… Feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: MIAODAM Exercise Wheel and Resistance Band

Marmot Slate Everyday Travel Bag This is a beautifully made daily backpack. I love the styling of it so much, and the materials are obviously high quality, extremely sturdy, and is made with care. It seems like it would be fairly rain resistant given the materials. However, a few things keep this from becoming my new favorite bag.

For one, there's no zipper on the top/main compartment which keeps all of your stuff in. While the fold over part seems to keep everything in, this anxiety kept me from wanting to bring it with me on a number of recent trips where I had things inside that were both small and valuable, such as my pen from my surface tablet. I also noticed that while the fabric looks very water repellent around the top, I found it hard to get it to scrunch inside perfectly so that I would be certain no water would come in. A zipper would have really been nice.

Second, the styling of the little chest strap that clips together the two shoulder straps when you are wearing it as a backpack for a little while, is diagonal. It doesn't look intentional, but I'm pretty sure it is. It makes it look like however I position it, my backpack appears to have shifted to a weird angle. It just gives my appearance and overall sloppy, poorly put together look that make it so I would not ever really want to use the chest strap and might as well cut it off.

Other than these quibbles, the bag is thoughtfully designed and beautifully made. The small pockets are just the right size and shape for the things I would want to use them for, the padding that keeps my back comfortable and would also be protective of a tablet or laptop is very thorough, though mildly stiff, and the styling of it aside from the chest strap is absolutely beautiful, very sleek and looks like a high-end daily backpack. If you don't need your backpack to zipper, and don't mind a diagonal chest strap, this is a beautiful choice to consider.
text_fidelity_b: Marmot Slate Everyday Travel Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Concept2 Model D Indoor Rowing Machine (Gray) This review is coming from a dumpy middle-aged woman with a hip replacement who *thought* she was going to buy a treadmill. I started comparison shopping for treadmills even though spending $1000 or more on a machine instead of just going outside for a walk seemed kind of ridiculous, even in the snow. Then I ran across an article that mentioned rowing machines as the best overall piece of home exercise equipment. Some of my college dorm mates rowed on the women's 8 and it was like the light went on. The unanimous glowing reviews for the Concept2 Model D sold me on this machine and I ordered it direct from Concept2.

After about a month I can recommend rowing without reservation. The machine itself is built like a tank. It took about 20 minutes to put it together and about 2 minutes to figure out how to separate the parts for storage. It takes about 20 seconds to actually pull the machine apart and tuck it away in a corner when I'm not using it, which I do every day. Separated, it takes up the floor space of a medium-sized refrigerator. Together, it's about 9 feet long and a possible trip hazard. I use it on a carpeted floor and haven't noticed any problems with slipping and the machine doesn't need to be leveled. Gunk tends to accumulate on the rollers under the seat, which would probably go unnoticed if you don't pull the sled off and tip it up, but it's easy to clean.

I spent the first week focusing on correct technique and not killing myself. The machine comes with two booklets, a memory card, and a bottle of chain oil. The Indoor Rowing booklet has a lot of good information on proper form and suggested workouts starting from your very first day. There are also videos and active user forums on the Concept2 website. I've been following the suggestions, started slowly, set the damper at 3 and have left it there. Most nights I row from 25 to 40 minutes followed by stretching (recommended: AM/PM Stretch with Madeleine Lewis or AM Yoga for Your Week with Rodney Yee). I spent a lot of time on form and kept my stroke rate at about 18-19 spm. Slow, right? But I don't get sloppy and as I get stronger it seems that upping the stroke rate doesn't really improve my performance all that much. Before I started rowing, the morning routine was to get out of bed with cramping in my thigh and buttocks that nearly put me in tears. No joke: this disappeared overnight as soon as I started rowing. I felt a little soreness, mostly in my upper back, but zero lower back pain and no cramping AT ALL. One week of this was worth the $900.

The rowing machine puts you in total control of your workout in terms of how hard and how fast you want to work, and doesn't require you to do anything other than row harder or faster - there's no incline or speed buttons to push like with a treadmill. The rowing motion feels quite natural to me and time slides by. I actually look forward to my rowing time, and even though I'm still just getting started there is nothing about this that makes me feel like I won't be looking forward to my rowing time any less by next year. Plus, I expect by then I will be getting a lot more competitive about upping my pace. Update: Concept2 has a 100,000m between Thanksgiving and Christmas challenge. UPS delivered the Monday after Thanksgiving and without even trying I'm within 15K with 4 days to go. That's how cool rowing is.

If you're on the fence about which home exercise machine to buy, do yourself a favor and buy a rowing machine. Do yourself an additional favor and buy a Concept2.
text_fidelity_b: Concept2 Model D Indoor Rowing Machine (Gray)

Nathan NS5113-0478-00 StrobeLight - Lime Punch/Classic Green A compact little visibility light, quite useful if you are running at night and want something to tell drivers that you are around. Superior to a simple reflective vest, especially with a blinking pattern. Not so useful at dusk though - the light simply isn't bright enough to draw a lot of attention when the ambient light is still high. This isn't a significant issue, just don't expect it to do something too substantial.

The interface is pretty good - a long press ensures that it will almost never be activated accidentally, it is easy to switch between modes, and the light remembers the last mode you were on. The blinking patterns are variegated and should draw notice from drivers. The clip is perfect for non-intrusive mounting to a belt, arm band, or pack strap.

I would recommend this for night runners, so long as it compliments a reflective vest and reflective wrist/ankle bands. I use it as a a rear pack light when hiking, since the pack hides my reflective vest. The lithium battery and long lifespan make this an ideal light to tuck away in your hiking pack just in case you end up on the road at night.

text_fidelity_a:
Travel Kuppe Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Cycling Sports Water Bottle, Includes Both Straw and Sip Lid If you must have a steel water bottle on your bicycle (for health or other reasons), this may be for you. However, there are many disadvantages. First, this bottle is big - about 1 inch taller than a 24 ounce plastic water bottle, even though the capacity is a smaller 20 ounces. Of course, this bottle is less efficient with space because of the insulation feature. The extra height will cause problems with smaller bicycles, especially in the seat tube water bottle cage. While the straw cap seems interesting, in practice this is useless on a bicycle. With the straw open, the bottle will not fit on my bicycle. With the straw closed, you need 2 hands to open the straw, which is dangerous while riding your bicycle. There are plastic insulated bicycle water bottles on the market that are much cheaper and lighter weight than this (eg Polar or Camelbak) and they don't need the straw since you can just squeeze them to squirt the water out.

This bottle is also very heavy - 11.5 ounces compared to 3 ounces for a standard plastic water bottle. Gripping this bottle is much more difficult than a plastic bottle since (1) it is slippery when wet and (2) it doesn't squeeze when gripped like a plastic bottle. I do not recommend using this bottle with metal water bottle cages since it rattles like crazy; a plastic water bottle cage may be better, especially if it has a grippy interior.

The insulation does work, but you only have 20 ounces of water in there so if you drink that in the first hour of your ride, can you refill the bottle with more cold water or just with tap water that isn't cold enough to be worth insulating? If you're not drinking at least 20 ounces per hour on a day that is hot enough to need an insulated water bottle, you are not drinking enough to avoid dehydration.

As a bicycle water bottle, I give this only 2 stars because of all the limitations. For use in a car's cup holder or similar it may work better, but then you're competing with dozens of other steel water bottles that cost much less, so I give it 2 stars for that use case as well.
text_fidelity_b: Travel Kuppe Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Cycling Sports Water Bottle, Includes Both Straw and Sip Lid

text_fidelity_a:
BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids. I purchased this to use on my bicycle that I use for commuting. I leave early in the morning while it is still dark. The route I take is pretty well lit with street lights so I use the lights mostly for visibility and not to light the road in front of me.

The mounts are pretty simple to use. I attached the front to the handlebar and the back to the basket I have on the rear rack. The front light has 3 steady settings at 3 levels of brightness and one flashing mode. I am not sure how useful the level of brightness would be in absolute darkness as far as seeing the path in front of you because I have not used it in that scenario, but it seems pretty bright to me. I keep it on flashing mode for visibility. It is conveniently re-chargeable via USB cord and it seems to last adequately between charges.

I gave this product a 3 star rating because the back light does not work the way I need it to. The first time I used it, I thought I turned it on but when I got to my destination it was off so I figured I forgot to turn it on. The second time I used it on the return trip, I made absolutely sure it was on when I started and when I got to the destination it was off again. I took the light off my bike and turned it on and dropped it onto a hard surface from a distance of less than 3 inches and it shut off. Since this is battery operated and not rechargeable, I'm guessing the batteries get jolted from going over a bump on the road and shuts off on its own. It lights up again without any issues if you press the on button again, but that is not feasible or safe to reach behind you and fix it if you are riding on a road with vehicular traffic all around you. It is also very inconvenient to pull over to the side every time it shuts off to turn it back on again. Since the light set was fairly inexpensive, I just purchased a different separate backlight from the local box store to replace it.

I will not go through the time and inconvenience of returning the item or exchanging it because it simply is not worth it. I hope the seller doesn't try to contact me to "fix" the problem because they will be wasting their time.
text_fidelity_b: BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids.

TYR Socket Rockets 2.0 Racing Goggle As with other swedish goggles, these require precise adjustment to create good seal. It is critical to realize that these goggles sit in the eye socket, not the orbit. The key really is the proper adjustment of the nosepiece: it really needs to be tighter than appears. I recommend substituting bungee strap in place of the latex strap provided - it is easier to adjust and gives better tension. Actually, once properly adjusted, the soft frame feels quite comfortable and, even after wearing them for about 35 minutes, they cause less eye pain than the usual "orbit" goggles. Nonetheless, I would not recommend these for "occasional" and inexperienced swimmers. Be extremely careful not to get hit in the face while wearing these.
I agree that they fog up quickly. This seems to be a chronic problem: every goggles I've owned fog up. You can solve the problem by using a defogger (I love Cressi anti-fog spray which I use when I go scuba diving) or, just use a bit of spit and rub it in - cheap and effective. Some say rubbing toothpaste (yes!!) followed by gentle rinsing also works.
text_fidelity_b: TYR Socket Rockets 2.0 Racing Goggle

Franklin Sports Cornhole Game Sets - Portable Cornhole Boards + Bean Bags - (2) Cornhole Boards + (8) Bean Bags Included - Perfect Beach + Lawn Tailgate Bean Bag Toss Game Set I tend to call this game "bean bags" but I guess "Cornhole" is the official name. It's a great game for a lazy afternoon with family or friends, or to set up when you're grilling. You set the tables up opposing each other and then take turns trying to throw your bean bags into the hole at the top/center of the table. Each player gets four shots. We usually score it three points if you get one in the hole and one if you get a bag on the table, but I haven't read the instructions to see what the "official" rules are. I'm sure every state has a regional variation of this game, and this set is good enough to play with whatever rules you want.

First of all, the tables are quite large. They measure about 2 feet by 4 feet wide. The tables have legs at the end with the hole that fold out so that they can be set up at an angle. I liked the material of these tables. I've played on sets that had a lot of give that allowed you to aim for the base of the table so your bean bag will slide right up into the hole. These sets feel sort of "dead" and your bean bag doesn't travel much. This requires a more skillful toss and it makes it harder to hit the hole. I like that because the result is fewer ties.

The carrying case is a large black bag with a zipper top. The tables fit into the bag, but it's kind of a tight fit. I tend to put the tables into the bag and then put the bean bags through the hole so that they sit between the tables. I have a Subaru Forester and the carrying case fits in that easily enough, but if you have a smaller car you might struggle bringing this set along to the beach. Also, it's a little awkward to carry, although it's not overly heavy.

If you're looking for a great cornhole set, this one is as good as anything out there. It sets up quick, packs away fast, and the carrying case helps protect the set while in storage. I like that it's labeled as a "professional" set, and it forces you to use good, precise tosses in order to win. Great fun at a grill, family gathering, or at the beach. Also, tossing bean bags is nice because if there are kids around they aren't going to get banged in the head by an errant horseshoe or something.

If you're looking for a family activity to help get your kids off their cell phones for a few minutes, look no further.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Cornhole Game Sets - Portable Cornhole Boards + Bean Bags - (2) Cornhole Boards + (8) Bean Bags Included - Perfect Beach + Lawn Tailgate Bean Bag Toss Game Set

Tents for Camping: Sportneer Tent for 2/3 Persons Family Pop Up Instant Tents Waterproof with Removable Top Rainfly Easy Set Up Tent 94.5"x86.6"x59" [[VIDEOID:64c8658b81382127e4a89d8e490ca985]] My kids love camping, so when we got this tent they were excited to try popping it up in our playroom first before we take it out. Before I go any further, I want to point out that to its' credit, this tent was easy enough for a couple of girls aged 9 and 11 to figure it out themselves.
That being said, I'm glad we did it at home first because I noticed at least one weird design flaw: The outer door cover is REALLY difficult to close from the inside. You see, like many tents, the doors are two layers: an outer rain flap and an inner bug-net window screen. bug net opens in the middle with a zipper, and the outer later opens on the sides (attached from the top, zipper around the perimeter).

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Cast Iron Grill Pan This 10" pre-seasoned cast iron grill pan by Coleman was offered at a very economical price as compared to similar items and meets the needs for which I intended to use it just fine. I needed a safe surface to do the final searing of sous vide steaks, chops and chicken for two so this is safe enough to handle the high intensity heat of the blow torch I use and sized is just right for a couple of steaks, chops, or chicken breasts at a time.

The sides are high enough to prevent my searing flame from flowing over the item and out of the pan area, the ribs contain the juices, and the pour spout makes draining easy. The handle is also cast iron so bear in mind that you need to wear oven mitts to protect your hands when cooking in the pan since it will get hot.

This pan is pre-seasoned, but that doesn't mean exactly the same thing as a non-stick coating. When it comes to cast iron pans, seasoning means a vegetable oil baked onto the iron at a high temperature which serves to protect the cast iron from moisture which would lead to the pan rusting, and also serves as a natural non-stick film for easy release of the item you're cooking.

You might want to add a little butter or oil if you're cooking eggs in the new pan however since the best non-stick benefits of seasoning haven't had a chance to really build up yet. After using this pan you should hand wash it, dry it completely, and then rub it with a light coating of vegetable oil on it to restore a sheen.

The more you use the pan and re-season it the better the non-stick tendency will be, and that's why a lot of folks love finding old cast iron pans at yard sales. Those old pans that were lovingly used & cared for over a long time had years to get well seasoned. If you take care of this one it should serve you well over the years so I'd gladly recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Cast Iron Grill Pan

The Inspire 2 is a smaller display and, depending on the templates you download on the app, can have more details showing on the home screen. There are a few things that I would complain about but are not major issues: first, there are 2 touch-sensitive nodes on the sides that seem to go off when my wrists are bent back and this happens very often which makes me think the notifications have gone off; the second is that I can’t adjust the vibration intensity on the watch so I miss phone calls and messages many times.

This is still a great buy if you only need the basics. All the features for heart rate, steps, and (this one shows) activity time are what you’re looking for when buying a watch like this.

Fitbit Charge 4 vs Inspire 2: What's the difference?
The Inspire 2 has a plastic body so it's a little cheaper in its appearance compared to the Charge 4. It also has a smaller touchscreen display than the Charge and it has a physical button on the side, making for a less streamlined design than the other two models.

Ultimately, it’s lightweight, compact, and doesn’t use up excessive power like other smartwatches on the market. It also charges pretty fast (20-30 minutes for a full charge) and it takes about 4-5 days to run out of power (2 days for smartwatches). I would definitely recommend that someone to buy it for fitness purposes.

Overall, an economical watch that does the job.

Cons: Fitbits stop working after a couple of years for no reason. This is my 4th one in the last 6 years.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire 2 Health & Fitness Tracker with a Free 1-Year Fitbit Premium Trial, 24/7 Heart Rate, Black/Rose, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

I have been infusing waters for a few years now, In the past year a number of infusing systems like this one have appeared so I am freed from the makeshift ones I used in the past. I received this one as a review sample and have more that a few others to which I can compare it.

The first thing I like is the capacity. It holds an ample 23 ounces of liquids and ingredients. That provides a lot of hydration when out and about. I do wish the infusing basket were a little longer to expose more of the infusing ingredients to the water, but for all practical purposes the one in this system is adequate.

The reason why I mentioned in the title that this one is perfect for beginners is it's easy to disassemble, is well sealed and leak proof, and easy to clean. I own some of the first generation infusers that are complicated and some are even made of glass. To be sure, those are perfect for we experienced infusers, but can be daunting to someone who is exploring the benefits. If you are new I recommend grabbing a copy of this excellent book: [[ASIN:B00IZ05F52 Fruit Infused Water - 80 Vitamin Water Recipes for Weight Loss, Health and Detox Cleanse)]]. It;s short, but packed with some good recipes that will get you started. Note: this bottle comes with an offer for a free ebook as well, I did not sign up for it because I have a personal policy of never joining a list in exchange for free information. You may want to check it out if you do order one of these.

Other reasons why I love this bottle is it's tough. It may be plastic, but I dropped mine and it did not crack. It's also BPA-free, which is a big deal for me. Finally, it's easy to hand wash.

Bottom line: if you want to explore the benefits of infusing waters this bottle is a nice, entry level system, Even if you are an experienced infuser this is worth looking into, Although the basket is too short in my opinion, the diameter is sufficient for mixing and matching ingredients. Plus I love having more than one bottle so I can grab one for short trips and to keep myself refreshed on breaks when performing.

JOOLA Infinity Balance - Advanced Performance Ping Pong Paddle - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for High-Level Training - Designed to Optimize Spin and Control (Method 38)

JOOLA Infinity Edge - Tournament Performance Ping Pong Paddle w/Pro Carbon Technology - Black Rubber on Both Sides - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for Advanced Training - Designed for Speed (Driver 42 Blue Handle)

JOOLA Infinity Edge - Tournament Performance Ping Pong Paddle w/Pro Carbon Technology - Black Rubber on Both Sides - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for Advanced Training - Designed for Speed (Driver 42 Red Handle)

JOOLA Omega Strata - Table Tennis Racket with Flared Handle - Tournament Level Ping Pong Paddle with Riff 34 Table Tennis Rubber - Designed for Spin .

It’s been years since I played Ping Pong and back then I never had the opportunity to use, and was not even familiar with the Joola brand unfortunately. As I have had time to use and play with these 5 different Joola Ping Pong paddles, I must say that they are all incredible compared to any other Ping Pong paddle I have ever used. The quality and performance far exceeds my previous experiences.

Each of these paddles have been designed for a specific purpose which include speed, spin and control. Now not being a professional, I can not “honestly” say that I notice the difference between any of these five different paddles, in any of the different design aspects while using them. However, I can honestly say that visually I can tell the difference by the different rubber padding (sandwiched between the inner and outer rubber) used in each. Some have a slightly different thickness, weight, color and I assume different “springiness”. With that said, each and every one of them have performed absolutely stellar in every way for my, and my family’s play style. Personally they all have incredible spin, speed and control capabilities. They are all built with beautiful build quality, and designed with comfort and balance in mind. I especially love the resin looking inlaid logo at the end of the handles. I realise that it doesn’t make a performance difference but it just ads to the overall beauty and gives each paddle a quality looking finish.

Overall I feel quite privileged to have had the opportunity to use and experience the Joola brand and share my opinions, though I feel absolutely unqualified to have done so. Just know that if you have never used or played with a “quality” Ping Pong paddle, you are truly missing out, and this Joola brand will be the only brand I choose from here on out! The quality is impeccable!!
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Infinity Balance - Advanced Performance Ping Pong Paddle - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for High-Level Training - Designed to Optimize Spin and Control

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Evanston Screened Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Weatherproof Tent with Roomy Interior Includes Rainfly, Carry Bag, Easy Setup and Screened-in Porch (WARNING- This is a long review. I am covering areas about this tent that were a concern to me. If you want a summary, go to the paragraph titled THE BOTTOM LINE)

I wanted to take the time to review this tent. I spent a LOT of hours researching, watching EVERY video and reading every available review I could find out there about this tent to decide which I would get. It was between this tent and [[ASIN:B001TSCF96 Coleman Montana 8-Person Tent]]. As it turned out, we had an immediate need for TWO tents, so I got both of them. You can see my review of the [[ASIN:B001TSCF96 Coleman Montana 8-Person Tent]] by clicking the link

WHAT IS THIS TENT LIKE?
One of the things I was concerned about was the thinness of material. We live in a very high elevation and get constant breezes or wind. There were a number of reviews that spoke of their tents snapping or ripping after only a gentle breeze. The fabric is thin, yes. But it does hold up.

Enough people have posted photos, so I won't post one as of yet. The best way to secure this tent is to ALWAYS leave the fly on. An unexpected storm or wind can come up at any time, and I personally feel that the tent is much more stable with the fly on than without. Make sure that you always stake down everything, including ALL of the ropes. That is what keeps the tent stable and secure.

FLOOR
The floor is very nice, and if you use a tarp underneath and take off shoes before entering, it will last quite a while. I also recommend not using chairs with small pointed feet on it either- it will wear out the floor quickly.

WINDOWS
The windows are perfect. They are protected from all but the most severe of rainstorms so you can leave them open if you like. The back window is open at all times, yes, but if staked down, it is not that big of a deal. If we plan to take this on crowded camp sites, I will sew two rings at either back seam and attach a thin fabric when changing. No big deal.

POCKETS AND LANTERN RING
The pockets are nice and in a good space. There is also a ring for hanging a lantern on if you like.

HEIGHT
The height is perfect for us- the tallest is 5 ft 9 inches. Taller people might not like this tent. The screened in porch is a bit narrow for those with long legs. You pretty much need a chair to use it unless you are a kid and don't need to lean back.

SCREENED IN PORCH
I LOVE this thing. I really do. This is my happy place. It is perfect for two camp chairs to look out at night or in the day. The door of the tent can stay open adding to a spacious feel. It does get wet in the rain. I am currently designing a fly to go over the porch and roll up into the tent when not in use. So far I am almost done with the one half of the fly and plan to finish the other half this week if I can. I hope to do that before the tent is taken down.

Without a fly, your stuff will get wet. There is an area that you can sweep the water into when wet, I use a sponge mop to clean it up so it will dry faster. Otherwise it puddles and does take a long time to dry.

POLES
The poles went up well for us, but you just have to take your time when putting up the tent. Do not race through the process, the fabric can rip if you don't.

TENT SPACE
Our biggest concern was ACTUAL usable space for us. We found that putting a queen inflatable double height mattress in there (Coleman) we have plenty of room for two of us. If using an additional single mattress, we can still do it, but it works best with a sleeping bag on the floor and picked up at night if a third person is in there (child).

When using or covering up the porch in rain, the porch makes a great extension for activities, talking, or just sitting and enjoying the view (if not raining). I absolutely love the design of this tent.

LIGHTING
The tent color is half of the beauty of this tent. The light bright colors are cheerful, let in a lot of light, and also keep it from feeling gloomy on rainy days. At night you can see through it, so keep that in mind when you are getting ready at night.

DOES THIS STAY UP IN STORMS?
The big question. I have an answer for you. We purchased this tent the week before Labor Day (US). We put the tent up immediately and treated it with silicone spray. We didn't need to- it is already made from silicone impregnated ripstop nylon. The seams also came pre-treated with silicone on the fly. AMAZING!.

We have had this tent up with daily use since then and it is now October 8,2016. So far it has been through extreme heat, breezes, high winds, thunder storms, all night rains, and heavy rain storms. The tent has stayed up with no observable damage at this point and stayed very dry too.

IMPORTANT POINTS
After reading MANY reviews on this tent, I decided to help it stay up, I would reinforce different areas. Anywhere that there is a plastic hook, I put a piece of garden twist tie into the fabric loop that holds the hook and tied it around the pole to help it absorb any shock of high winds. Any other plastic rings or hooks were reinforced in the same way. I tucked the ends of the twist tie way under so no chance of the fabric blowing into sharp edges and tearing in high winds.

STAKES
I also recommend getting other stakes for the tent. They stay in the ground during storms more easily too. I got [[ASIN:B01IEBKK92 Pack of 16, 7075 Aluminum Outdoors Tent Stakes & Rubber Hammer & Guyline Tensioner with Reflective Pull Cords & Carrying Pouch]] to use in the fly staking process, and used the ones that came with the tent for the actual tent staked to the ground.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Honestly, this is my favorite tent of all time. It is my happy place. I absolutely LOVE the design, set up, colors, and ventilation of this tent. With a mattress, it is still private to lay down with the windows open and you can still look out at the sky and enjoy the scenery. When you are in the tent and want to have breeze, the front door open makes it seem so airy and wonderful. I can not rave about this tent enough. Five weeks of constant use is more than we planned for, but it has held up so far.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED at five stars.

QUESTIONS AND UPDATES
If you have any questions I have not answered, by all means ask. I hope I can be helpful, as I know how it helps me when others do the same. I will update with any more input should I have anything else to share or if there are problems with the tent.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Evanston Screened Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Weatherproof Tent with Roomy Interior Includes Rainfly, Carry Bag, Easy Setup and Screened-in Porch

text_fidelity_a:
Bowflex TC5000 Treadclimber (Discontinued) Bottom line is, if someone asked me if I would 'recommend', I would pause and struggle. Well...I wouldn't NOT recommend..afterall, I do sweat in a hurry; it does get your heart going; it doesn't take up much space; it is built well; it does give you a few variations of usage. Unfortunately, I can't comment on what results I get because I don't USE IT enough to really know. By the same token, I cannot comment on anything mechanical either, for the same reason.

We all have our own reasons for NOT using something and certainly most can relate to having fitness equipment that collects dust, or clothes! So when friends or family members ask me why I don't use mine, other than all the personal excuses, the reasons are this:

I find that I have to be so careful how I walk and how I place each and every step I make on this machine, or it occasionally twists my knee around. I cannot explain it in writing, but it's so frequent that it does this that I spend all my time concentrating on walking so that I'm unaffected! If I don't, I have had it jerk my knee, my ankles and it of course affects everything on up - back, hips, etc.
It doesn't seem to make any difference whether I use the treadles, or lock them together to use as treadmill. In fact, when I use the treadles, I find that i have to walk with somewhat of a straddle to give equal weight proportion to the motion otherwise your motion is something equivalent to walking with one high heel shoe on and one off. So, the very way that you step manipulates the treadles.
All this completely takes away from enjoying the use of the machine and it becomes a chore for me. I have other things I want to concentrate on than each and every step I make, and being so cautious! I mean, who wants that?!

Funny, I have read every review and every comment and don't see anyone else mentioning these things and I'm not sure why not. My sister and a friend jumped on my machine and they could completely see what I was talking about. Is it just my machine? I don't know. I purchased mine directly from Bowflex and paid a bundle more than this price showing on Amazon, btw!

Again, it isn't that I DON'T recommend this item, but for me, anyway, I would probably get more enjoyment, more usage, and therefore greater results, for FAR LESS money using something else.
text_fidelity_b: Bowflex TC5000 Treadclimber (Discontinued)

Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack-Red-L My husband was looking for a day pack. I bought him 6 backpacks to compare. The [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]], the [[ASIN:B00DNTR5CQ Osprey Packs Momentum 22 Daypack (Spring 2016 Model), Carbide Grey]], the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]], the [[ASIN:B00FUWSTI8 Lightweight Rucksack 25L for men women kids - Foldable into Inner pocket (BLACK)]], the [[ASIN:B013K7CJD0 Cycling Hiking Backpack Sunhiker Water Resistant Travel Backpack Lightweight SMALL Daypack M0714 (Dark Green)]], and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. There were pros and cons for each pack. He decided to keep the [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]]because it met his needs the best. We ordered all packs in gray, green, or black. We returned the other 5 packs. I liked 2 of the lightweight foldable packs - the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]]and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. I decided to order those for myself in Pink and Purple.
All of the packs had a mesh pocket on each side of the pack for water bottles. We tested them all with a Nalgene bottle and a bottle of water. All of the packs could easily hold the bottle of water. Some were a very tight fit for the Nalgene bottles. All packs had a main compartment with one or two pockets in the front of the pack. The main compartments varied from 561 cubic inches to 1386 cubic inches. 3 of the packs were lightweight, foldable, and storable in their own pocket.
Here are my summaries of this pack:
825 cubic inches
16 1/2” x 10” x 5”
6” mesh pockets – smaller pockets
Covers about 4 ¾” of bottles
Straps 2 ¼” wide
This pack has 3 main compartments. In the back is the largest zippered compartment. In the middle is a middle sized zippered compartment. In the front is a small zippered pocket.
Pros:
- Small zippered pocket inside the main compartment. This is where the pack is stored when folded.
- Very easy to adjust shoulder straps
- Reinforced mesh straps feel soft and pliable
- Pockets fit a Nalgene bottle
- Handle at top of pack for an additional way of carrying pack
Cons:
- Thinner material than a standard backpack.
- No back padding and did not keep it’s shape. Typical for a foldable pack.

I ordered one of these for myself in a different color.

SCHWINN Crewmaster Rower 100660, Gray We have a Schwinn recumbent bike that's held up well over the years, so were excited to try a Schwinn rower. This arrived well-packed in a series of boxes (be prepared to have a lot of packing materials to deal with), and it took about an hour to unpack and assemble, at least with two people. There's two main pieces that are heavy, and everything is included to put it together (other than something sharp to cut up the boxes, ties and packaging. There's a metal bar you need to remove from the front to put the 'stabilizer' in place, probably to keep anything from bending while in transit.
The motion is smooth once everything is together and the resistance is adjustable, which is good because you'll be able to use the equipment for a while.
You definitely need a pair of shoes while working out because of the position of the screws, and the screen/monitor is a little on the cheap side (it's powered by batteries and doesn't have a lot of options other than keeping track of your workout).
The long 'track' bar can bend upward to 'save' space or allow the machine to be moved about, but it still takes up a good bit of space and is heavy, so I don't think everyone will be able to move this about. But it is a good rowing machine and it does provide a great workout.

text_fidelity_a: MUSE S: The Brain Sensing Headband - Overnight Sleep Tracker & Meditation Headset Device - Multi Sensor Monitor with Responsive Sound Feedback Guidance from Brain Wave, Heart, Body & Breath Activity As a lifelong insomniac I was genuinely excited by this product. With practice it held the promise of assisting  with sleep as well as helping with meditation. The product comes in two long boxes. One holds the headband while the other contains the sensing device and charging cable (no charger is included). Set up is simple and pairing with the app initially was fine. The app is colorful and easy to navigate. The first issue came with positioning the headband. It is made somewhat stretchy material. The sensors must be in contact with the users skun. Not an issue for the ones on the forehead but the ear ones are a problem. I have kong hair and eventually wound up fashioning a sloppy top knot to keep it out of the way. Even then if is temperamental and I spend an inordinate amount of time fussing with it. Once it is correctly positioned you can move on to either meditations, sleep based meditations or your information. The ones included are fairly basic and easy to follow. The sounds indicate whether you are calm, neutral or active. I found the sounds intrusive. It helped to reduce the volume. I also question the accuracy. During one session my foot fell asleep and while I was rubbing and shaking out the pins and needles all was quiet with birds chirping. Seems that is when the weather should have been bad. Then when I was absolutely still and silent it stormed. So I don't have much face in their real time monitoring. It was during the sleep portion that I encountered multiple disconnects and finally just gave up. Similarly when downloading the meditations I run into the technical difficulties, try again nonsense. I use mine with a tablet and it helps to either use the sleeping amber light or to dim down the device lights. I have not found the sleep portion conducive to rest. It ends in a jarring manner. Following a yoga nidra meditation on YouTube is far more helpful. Checking the results is fun even though I take them with a grain of salt. The rechargeable battery has goid life lasting between eight to ten hours before requiring a recharge. I do wish they would straighten out the connection issues and include a case for the band and unit. When it works without interruption it is fun and a good way to master the monkey mind. But the constant interruptions are disruptive and frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: MUSE S: The Brain Sensing Headband - Overnight Sleep Tracker & Meditation Headset Device - Multi Sensor Monitor with Responsive Sound Feedback Guidance from Brain Wave, Heart, Body & Breath Activity

text_fidelity_a:
SKLZ Reactive Catch Trainer for Improving Hand-Eye Coordination & Speed I assumed this was a bit gimmick and didn't have high hopes. Kiddo is going to be 9 next month and his catch skills are terrible. He and his dad have been working on it, but he is much better at throwing a ball then catching one. He also does well with footwork like in soccer, but man the catching is just sad. I try to help by tossing him small things in the house and usually they just land on the floor and he gives me an irritated "What the heck mom" look. Err, he also has taken several softballs and footballs to the face, when they practice outside, eeek.

So I saw this and figured it couldn't hurt. We played a slow paced soft toss indoor version with the three of us for him to get the hang of it. The tosser would name a color, then give a gentle underhand lob (no spin) and the catcher would have to grab that color. The next day the two of them took it outside for a bit more distance and because I didn't want things getting broken...

Fast-forward a week and I toss a tinfoil ball to him to throw away and he snatches it with one hand (his left no less, he's a righty) like some sorta ninja. Now I'm not saying its not also part luck but there is NO WAY that would have happened a week ago. The look on his face was all smiles instead of the usual glare I get when I toss him stuff and it hits the floor.

This really does help the brain relearn catching to focus on the item to catch rather than the one tossing it. His confidence boost has also been a big help in getting him to want to practice catching in general.

I'm one happy momma and give this a very enthusiastic 5 stars, particularly if you have kiddo in need of some help with catching.
text_fidelity_b: SKLZ Reactive Catch Trainer for Improving Hand-Eye Coordination & Speed

WILD MAN Bike Bag, Bike Accessories, Bike Phone Holder Bike Phone Mount, Waterproof Bike Phone Bag, Mountain Bike Accessories for Adult Bikes with 3D Hard EVA, TPU Touch Screen and Sun Visor for Phones Under 6.7" This is a sort of gem in a way considering I have never heard of the brand. The quality is fantastic to the point where you could easily mistake this for an expensive, established brand. AND...even though Wild Man is or is not a good name, at least it makes sense, more or less, for a bike accessory.

Anyway, it seems like they got everything right, but just be advised that this is NOT the type of case where you can see your phone through the top, despite saying it's compatible with all these devices; that's just a way to add search terms, and I guess it's technically correct that those phones will fit in this bag.

While I haven't had this out in a downpour, it has what appear to be excellent quality, self-sealing zippers on the exterior that should be essentially waterproof as far as rain goes (likely not submersible). It's sort of a "shell" case in that it is semi-rigid, and the material has a checkered carbon fiber look to it, which is neat looking and will likely match a lot of fancier bikes, but will work with anything since it's basically black.

The three straps come large enough that I imagine they can be used with any bike, and can be adjusted down as necessary; I expect the cleanest and nicest installations will involve trimming the excess. The one strap is "across" the opening of the two sections, which would limit how far you can open it, except there is a piece of fabric inside artificially limiting how far you can open it, perhaps so that the former's limitation is not so obvious, but I suspect it will help keep you from dropping stuff out of the case while it is installed on the bike.

One side is a half-height net, and the other side is a full height zippered net, both of which offer some stretch, and are very much like a good piece of luggage.

This definitely adds a little bulk to your bike, and I'm not convinced everyone will want on for permanent storage (there are lots of other placement options to consider), but I can imagine that this goes quite far when doing multi-day riding with camping stops. The great thing is that it can be taken off and put back on quite easily, and as needed.
text_fidelity_b: WILD MAN Bike Bag, Bike Accessories, Bike Phone Holder Bike Phone Mount, Waterproof Bike Phone Bag, Mountain Bike Accessories for Adult Bikes with 3D Hard EVA, TPU Touch Screen and Sun Visor for Phones Under 6.7"

text_fidelity_a:
Zefal 164 Water Bottle, 33 oz I do like having these bottles for bikepacking. It makes the difference between having to carry some kind of bladder vs making the jump between towns in the middle of summer during midday. The 1L capacity is the big appeal for me.

For me, the Camelback Podium water bottles are the best I've used. I would rate the Podium at 4 stars. I've gotten used to the annoyances and now I have really on positive associations with that water bottle .

This Zefal bottle gets additional points for capacity, and loses many points for the following criteria:
Distinct plastic taste that appears very quickly. With my other water bottles, I detect some leeching only when I leave water in the bottle overnight or longer. With the Zefal, it's almost immediate. That worries me.

Requires too much force to seal the lid. On my first bikepacking trip with these, I kept wasting water because my first squeeze after each stop would go on my face and jersey, in addition to my mouth. I'm used to it now and I know how hard I need to muscle on the lids.

No jet nozzle. This is the same basic design as water bottles had 40 years ago. It's not horrible - it works like it's supposed to; OTOH if the Camelback is 4 stars then this design is worth much less.

Branding: I simply feel strange about branding on really low-end items. IDK - maybe I'm afraid that people with think that I think this is great water bottle? Maybe I shouldn't take that out on the product. I definitely don't mind the Camelback logo, no matter how outlandish and counter to my design taste, and yet with these bottles even the conservative branding seems to be in bad taste.

Overall, this bottle simply fails to meet my criterion for good cycling gear: its interface/use is not transparent. I.e. instead of simply using it routinely / out of habit / on muscle memory, I'm always aware of opening the valve, tasting plastic, and remembering to close the valve as I return it to the cage. Gear that I consider over the threshold for good sinks down out of sight much faster than my habit formation with these - assuming I will ever get used to them. At this point it seems more likely that next summer I'll set out of find a better solution to this same problem.

I simply don't like these bottles.

Overall this feels like many levels of quality down from the Camelback bottles. I find the capacity appealing and really nothing else. It's like the quip about cookie-cutter, drywall box "McMansion": it's not home, but it's much.
text_fidelity_b: Zefal 164 Water Bottle, 33 oz

text_fidelity_a:
EBAT LED Lantern Recharged by solar panel+USB Cable for Travel, Picnic, Hiking, Yellow [[VIDEOID:7cace53d54dd11d9ca86d52ec20f0527]] If you ever go camping or if you live in an area where there are frequent power outages you understand the need for a good lantern. I have worked with several lanterns and while I have used some that are a little brighter or a little more compact, this one is a decent one that has some good features. Besides having a couple of operation modes, it is chargeable via solar energy.

This is a reasonably bright lantern but it is not blindingly bright like some others I have seen. This is a trade-off in my book. If you are expecting something that is bright enough to light a small camp area and allow you to read by it, this is a decent lamp. If you want something to light a 20'x20' room it is not strong enough to provide color recognition through the whole room.

This lantern has a rechargeable battery that can be removed and plugged in to the provided power adapter for recharging. It can also be opened up to expose a pair of solar panels so it can be charged up via solar power. There is something very important to understand about solar charging, though – using the solar panels to charge this lantern takes a lot longer than if plugging the pack in. I have not tried to completely charge the lantern via solar power but in my experience solar charging takes roughly 4 to 5 times longer. That said, if you do not have the option to plug in, the solar panel is a superb option.

This lantern seems to be solidly made and resistant to easy breakage. So, I believe it would survive a drop from a short distance, though I would hesitate to test this theory. The hook loop on top is plastic but it seems sturdy enough to handle frequent use and abuse.

This lantern has two operation modes. It has two brightnesses – dim and bright. The dim light is enough to light a hallway when carrying this lantern though it is not going to work for tromping through the woods. The bright setting is not actually all that bright but it is enough to see through a large room and make out everything in it, though it does not cast enough light to see colors clearly at more than 10' or so.

Overall, this is a decent little lantern. It seems to be made well and it can be charged by either a power adapter or solar power. Just keep in mind that it is not going to charge quickly if using the solar cells to charge it up.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: EBAT LED Lantern Recharged by solar panel+USB Cable for Travel, Picnic, Hiking, Yellow

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I have been wanting a Fitbit for a really long time.  I did some research because I was not sure which one I wanted.  I went to the website and read about them all.  This one had all the features that I wanted.  I never wear a watch and my cell phone is too big to fit in my pocket while I work out.  So it was important for me that I could view time with my Fitbit.  Just a tap of the screen and I can view the time.  Or I can just flick my wrist and the time displays.  Or I can press the button on the side.  The Fitbit HR is thicker than what I would have liked, but it is not worth giving it less than 5 stars over that.  I can view my steps and check my heart rate.  Many reviews have said that the heart rate is not accurate.  Honestly that is not a feature that was a make it or break it to me.  I don't know if the heart rate is accurate or not.  The Fitbit also lets me know how many miles I have walked. It also tracks if I went up any flights of steps or not. I can even use it as an alarm.  It just vibrates gently.  Setting up the Fitbit and syncing it to my Android phone was a breeze.  The app is great.  The Fitbit HR also tracks my sleep patterns.  I can set challenges for myself and even challenge others.  The first day I set up a challenge to take 10,000 steps.  Throughout the day whenever I am near my phone with my Fitbit on, they sync and update.  I got special badges for being close to my goal.  It really encouraged me to make sure that I got to my 10,000 steps.  With the app I can log how much water I have drank and how many calories I have eaten and how many I have left.  My husband loves my Fitbit HR and really wants one for himself.  The directions say not to take a shower or go swimming in it.  That is perfectly fine with me.  I just take it off when I take a shower.  I am glad that I went ahead and purchase my Fitbit HR.

Backyard Champs Cornhole Carry Bag If you own a cornhole set, you are well aware of the need to transport the set from your garage to your backyard, basement to car, etc. You could just carry the boards and bean bags the way they are, but a better option is to store the set in a carrying bag. And a good choice for the task is the Backyard Champs 2 x 4 Cornhole Carry Bag.

I got hold of this bag at the same time that I obtained a cornhole set, also from Backyard Champs. The idea of a carrying bag made sense, so I added it to my order. The bag is black in color and seals shut with Velcro flaps. It measures two feet in width, four feet in length, and eight inches in thickness. Thus, it has enough space to hold the cornhole set I own, which is from the same company. However, it may not be the correct size for other sets, so make sure you measure first.

The carrying handles on this bag are a little thinner than expected. They are also looped more widely than I feel they should be. A little less width, more like a briefcase handle, would seem better. The cornhole set I have isn’t too heavy so I think the handles will hold up, but there is still a little more looseness than I prefer. I hope I am proven wrong and that the manufacturer knew what they were doing when they designed the bag, but it just seems a little too loose for me. I suppose they made the loop larger so that you can place the handle over your shoulder but I prefer to carry it more like a suitcase.

Cornhole sets are often bulky and they need to be protected when transporting from one place to another. A carrying bag makes sense and the Backyard Champs 2 x 4 Cornhole Carry Bag is a good choice for the task. A little more snug fit and a separate compartment for the bean bags would make this bag better, but it is a good enough bag for the job.
